utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also among the refugee families there was Bilal and Mirsad who were members of the army.

utterances.speaker: I didn't quite understand.  You told us that you were a member
utterances.text: Could you repeat the names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Refugees from Sokolac, Milavica Mirsad and Milavica Bilal. They were also members of the Territorial Defence of Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: I didn't quite understand.  You told us that you were a member
utterances.text: I don't know them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that on that day, that is, the 18th of May, and then again the next day, on the 19th of day, you saw this group of soldiers who had come with these green scarves. That was an exceptional event and that is why you remembered it so well, because those men were not in Kakanj before. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: I didn't quite understand.  You told us that you were a member
utterances.text: Earlier on I would see one or two sitting, a Mujahedin or a MOS Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. member in camouflage and with those scarves, but on that day there was a van driving round Kakanj, shouting, yelling, carrying rifles. But in those days there were big posters saying that people were not allowed to wear even uniforms if they were not members of military units. And never mind weapons. They were supposed to leave their weapons on the front or to the place of deployment. If I am at number 7, I go to number 7. And everyone knew who went where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. On the 19th of May, as you said in answer to a question from the Prosecution, in front of your house on a meadow, some 200 metres away from you perhaps, you noticed this group talking to a man in uniform; is that right?

utterances.speaker: I didn't quite understand.  You told us that you were a member
utterances.text: There's no 200 metres there. I'm sorry. It may be perhaps -- well, let's say not even 60 or 70 metres away. It's right nearby. 200 metres may be the distance up to the last house over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, in your statement you gave to the Prosecutor, you said that between your house and the house in which Enver Hadzihasanovic family was staying was about 250 to 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: I didn't quite understand.  You told us that you were a member
utterances.text: We are talking about houses. But you asked me about the meadow where these soldiers were. That's a different matter. The house is one thing, and the spot where the soldiers were is another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't hear any -- anything of the conversation that was going on between that man and these soldiers.

utterances.speaker: I didn't quite understand.  You told us that you were a member
utterances.text: I couldn't hear anything, because I was looking through my window. I could see some gesturing with their hands. I didn't hear words, but it is true that I saw them. And then -- I'm sorry. I don't know what you were asking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've clarified that. You couldn't hear it. You saw them from a distance that you indicated. The next day in the morning, that is, on the 20th of May, you had decided to go to the house where the wife and two small children of Enver Hadzihasanovic were living; is that right?

utterances.speaker: I didn't quite understand.  You told us that you were a member
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you inquired with the neighbours to point out the house.

utterances.speaker: I didn't quite understand.  You told us that you were a member
utterances.text: I didn't ask the neighbours, because I knew where the row of houses was. I know it was one of the three or four. But once I got there, I would ask somebody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. When you arrived nearby, you asked somebody to tell you.

utterances.speaker: I didn't quite understand.  You told us that you were a member
utterances.text: No, I didn't, because I didn't see anyone in the street except in front of one house there was a table and a soldier, and I asked him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Before I move on to my next question, the soldiers that you saw in the meadow, you didn't see any insignia that may have been worn by those soldiers except for those green bandannas on their heads.

utterances.speaker: I didn't quite understand.  You told us that you were a member
utterances.text: I saw on those soldiers -- I had seen them in Kakanj the day before, and I saw them wearing bandannas. I knew that they were the same ones. They had all kinds of wording, "The MOS," on them. Because they passed by my house, maybe a couple of steps away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you reached that house, you said that in the garden you saw soldiers sitting at a table; is that right?

utterances.speaker: I didn't quite understand.  You told us that you were a member
utterances.text: It isn't a garden. It was in front of the house. On the pavement or on the small piece of land in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But at the time you didn't see the wife or the children of Enver Hadzihasanovic.

utterances.speaker: I didn't quite understand.  You told us that you were a member
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see Enver Hadzihasanovic there either.

utterances.speaker: I didn't quite understand.  You told us that you were a member
utterances.text: No, I didn't. He wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The soldier that you did see, you didn't know him at all, did you?

utterances.speaker: I didn't quite understand.  You told us that you were a member
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before giving the floor to the other Defence team, a Judge of the Chamber has a question for the witness. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RASOAZANANY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, let us go back to the moment when you were at Kraljeva Sutjeska before going to Vares. And you told the Chamber that there were people who were burning cars and goods. I want to know who were those people that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: I didn't quite understand.  You told us that you were a member
utterances.text: In Poljane, where these people had gathered, they were Croats who were fleeing from the surrounding villages. And their property in question was their personal property, tractors and trucks. As the BH Army had cut across or blocked the main road -- in fact, the only road that was passing through Kraljeva Sutjeska, and they couldn't use their vehicles, and so as not to let the army get hold of that property, they set fire to those vehicles. There were quite a number of tractors, passenger cars on fire. And then they all took the route towards Planica where Serb positions were, and we crossed those Serb positions. We went through Serb positions to reach Vares.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I should like to give the floor to the other Defence counsel for the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, there are no questions that we have for this witness. I'm grateful, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Dixon. I turn now to the Prosecution to ask them whether they have any additional questions in view of the questions put by the Defence counsel within the framework of their cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution has no re-examination for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Witness, you came at the request of the Prosecution to testify. You have answered questions put to you by the parties and the Judges. We wish to thank you for your testimony, and we wish you a safe return trip. We hope that the climactic conditions will allow you to go home quickly. And as you're coming from Germany, I don't think that you will be having any major problems. I will ask the usher to accompany you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Now, let me ask the Prosecution to inform us about the weather forecast and the arrival of the witness that we're all expecting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I would be glad if I could inform you about the weather forecast, but I can tell you that the witness who is scheduled for tomorrow has arrived and he will be called tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. That is good news. Then we'll be able to complete the hearing of the witnesses for this week. It seems to me that there's another outstanding matter to address, and that is the CDs. I saw some being passed around a moment ago. Is the Prosecution going to tender into evidence the CD-ROM containing the video clips of the witnesses we heard yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honour, in order to discuss this issue, may I please ask to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was what I was going to suggest. Let us go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As it is 5.30, we have no more witnesses, we will adjourn and we will see all the parties again tomorrow at 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 30th day of January, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.31 p.m.,
